> **Purpose:** a single document summarizing whether this project succeeded, with numbers —
> not impressions. This is what sponsors/stakeholders read when they do not have time to open 100
> documentation files, and what the next project references when estimating timeline/budget.
> **Fill after:** Release complete + BAST signed (if applicable).

## 4. Deliverables — Final Checklist

Reference `docs/pm/BAST.md` for detail; confirm final status here.

```
□ Source code delivered (if per contract)
□ Release notes sent
□ User manual sent (if applicable)
□ Technical documentation complete and archived
□ BAST signed (client-facing) or closure confirmed (internal)
□ Temporary credentials/access revoked — see §8
```

### 4a. Project Closure Documentation Package (must be verified complete)

Before the project is marked complete, ensure these six documents exist, are final, and are archived
together — this is the minimum package that must be delivered/stored at project closure, not just
"if there is time":

```
□ Project Charter (docs/pm/PROJECT-CHARTER.md) — approved final version
□ Project specification documentation — Wireframe / PRD / FSD (docs/planning/FSD.md, PRD.md,
  docs/architecture/WIREFRAMES.md) — reflecting what was actually built, not initial drafts
□ User manual (deliverable to client, if updated in the last release)
□ UAT result (docs/planning/REQUIREMENTS-SIGNOFF.md — results and UAT sign-off, not just
  "UAT complete")
□ Actual timeline report (docs/pm/MILESTONE-REGISTER.md + §2 above — plan vs actual)
□ BAST (docs/pm/BAST.md) — handover acceptance report, if client-facing
```

**If any of these is incomplete, do not close Gate C.** Documentation that "will be completed later"
after the team moves to the next project usually never gets finished — and this is the package
most often searched for again during disputes or when a similar project starts.

| Team health during project (burnout, overtime) | {…} | {…} |

**Average score:** {…} / 5

> Score is not to punish the team — it is for patterns. If "team health" is consistently low across
> several consecutive projects, that is a signal to review at the planning level
> (buffer/estimation), not to blame a single project.

## 8. Post-Project Security & Access

```
□ Third-party API credentials used during development have been rotated
□ Temporary access (contractor, vendor, external agent) has been revoked
□ Test/dummy accounts in production have been deleted or deactivated
□ Database/server credentials have been transferred to the new maintenance holder (if changed)
```

> This is the most common cause of post-project security gaps — access shared for temporary
> purposes and never revoked. Do not postpone this section to "later".
